messages:
Sam Park: oncall-bot just paged me for high request 5xxs hitting the text-gen frontends — looks correlated with a spike in tail latency on gpu-pool-eu-west. seeing ~10% 5xx for a 20m window. rolling mitigation now.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT_TRIGGERED: high_5xx_rate (sev:pg) — channel: #eng-oncall — incident id: INC-2026-032 — paging Sam Park, Maria Chen

Maria Chen: on it, re-routing a subset of traffic to fallback smaller model in eu-west cluster to reduce memory pressure. gating the switch behind canary (5%) first.

Ashley R.: logs show a lot of KV-cache misses during the spike. eviction churn metric for kv-store-2 spiked at the same time. suspecting a mis-sized LRU window after a recent rollout.

Sam Park: good find. starting graceful fallback: set routing policy to prefer model-quantized-v2 for non-critical routes. runbook step: 
```
# quick deploy via infra bot
infra-bot deploy-route --route /generate --model model-quantized-v2 --weight 0.15
```

oncall-bot: Reroute started — canary 15% set. observability hooks linked: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/latency-overview

Jorge V.: putting a throttle on retries at the gateway to avoid request storms while cache warms up: added 50ms backoff and max 2 retries.

Maria Chen: after reroute and retry throttle, 5xxs are trending down to baseline. KV eviction rate still elevated but hit rate recovering slowly.

Ashley R.: from the debug dumps: a recent client-side change increased typical seq-length and changed request key variance which ended up polluting the prefix cache. we should add a quick alert for sudden changes in median seq-length per route.

Sam Park: agreed. also we need to tune alerting — this pager woke us up for a transient blip. propose we change the 5xx alert to fire only if >=5% for 15m AND total QPS > 200. reduces noise for low-traffic windows.

Maria Chen: +1. I'll open a PR with the new prometheus alert rule and add a note to the incident.

Sam Park: also request a short-lived dashboard card for KV cache hit rate by route, and an eviction-rate alert: fire when evictions/sec > 50 for 5m AND hit_rate < 85%. we need both magnitude and quality checks.

Ashley R.: drafting grafana panel and alert rule. query I'm using for the hit rate: 
```
sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{pool=~"kv-store-.*"}[5m]))
/
sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool=~"kv-store-.*"}[5m]))
```
panel notes: split by route tag, heatmap for per-route hit rate.

Sam Park: good. include a visualization for key eviction churn: 
```
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="kv-store-2"}[1m])
```
Add a recording rule to smooth spikes: kv_cache_evictions_1m = increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])

Maria Chen: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-alerts/pull/412 — changes: 5xx alert threshold + qps gating, new median-seq-length alert, eviction alert, new grafana dashboard json.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: mitigated — 5xx rate returning to baseline, canary stable. duration so far: 28m. incident status: monitoring.

Lee Kim: starting handoff — I'm next oncall in 15m. Sam, anything critical to watch after you sign off?

Sam Park: watch eviction-rate and median-seq-length for the next 2 hours. if eviction-rate > 100 sustained for 10m then escalate to eng-runtime. Also verify the scheduled job that rebuilds prefix caches isn't overlapping with heavy traffic windows — that's a configuration change we should avoid.

Maria Chen: added a temporary maintenance window blocking the cache rebuild cron for 2h. I also added a runbook note: when eviction alerts fire, check client seq-length variance and recent client deploys first.

Jorge V.: I'll follow up with client-team slack to confirm they didn't deploy a change that increased key variance. pinging them now.

Ashley R.: new dashboard uploaded to shared folder: https://grafana.redwood.internal/dashboards/kv-cache-ops — includes per-route hit-rate, eviction rate, median seq-length, and a compact panel for model routing weights. I've added alert annotations on the five recent spikes for context.

Sam Park: thanks. I'm going to sign off in 10. leaving a short summary in #incidents. feel free to escalate if any of the tuned alerts fire.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED? not yet — monitoring only. next update automatically in 30m.

Lee Kim: thanks Sam, taking over. I'm pinning the grafana dashboard and subscribing to the eviction alert. can someone add me to the infra-alerts PR review?

Maria Chen: added Lee as reviewer. also left a code comment about the qps gating value, let's tune after a day of telemetry.

Sam Park: ":thumbsup:" leaving handover summary: mitigation: canary reroute to model-quantized-v2, gateway retry throttle, temp cache rebuild block, alerts adjusted (5xx gating + eviction alert + median-seq-length), new dashboard. no customer-facing impact observed after mitigation.

Lee Kim: acknowledged. I'll keep watch and if nothing else in 2h I'll mark incident as resolved.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: Sam Park -> Lee Kim at 1840003520

Maria Chen: post-incident action items saved to incident tracker: INC-2026-032 -> add long-term fixes: better cache sizing simulation, per-route TTLs, and client SDK guidance to reduce key variance.

Sam Park: thanks team, good work moving fast.
